economic_curvature_intensity.apply: row's bin -> its |curvature| (Stage 2: rounded IntervalIndex categories; Stage 3: exact numeric edges); ECI = mean of the three
economic_curvature_intensity.fallback: outside the bins or an empty bin: 0.0
economic_curvature_intensity.fit: for each of euribor3m, nr.employed, emp.var.rate: qcut(20, duplicates='drop') of the fit rows, rate per non-empty bin, |np.gradient(np.gradient(rates))| over the non-empty bins (zeros if fewer than 3)
economic_curvature_intensity.fit_rows_in_their_own_representation: yes, through its bin's rate and its neighbours'
economic_curvature_intensity.smoothing: none; each curvature combines the rates of up to five neighbouring bins

neighborhood_subscription_density.apply: Gaussian kernel (bandwidth 1.0, scaled space) over the reference rows: sum_j K_j y_j / (sum_j K_j + 1e-10)
neighborhood_subscription_density.fallback: none (every row gets a kernel average)
neighborhood_subscription_density.fit: StandardScaler on (euribor3m, nr.employed, emp.var.rate) of ALL fit rows; reference = 5,000 fit rows drawn with default_rng(42) when the fit has more than 10,000 rows (every production fit does), else every fit row
neighborhood_subscription_density.fit_rows_in_their_own_representation: only a reference row (5,000 of the fit rows), with weight K(0) / sum_j K_j
neighborhood_subscription_density.smoothing: the kernel; only reference rows' labels contribute

subscribe_rate_by_dow_month.fallback: a cell absent from the fit rows: the global rate
subscribe_rate_by_dow_month.fit: global = mean label of the fit rows; per cell day_of_week x month (string key, years pooled): (n_cell * mean_cell + 100 * global) / (n_cell + 100)
subscribe_rate_by_dow_month.fit_rows_in_their_own_representation: yes: 1/(n_cell + 100) through the cell plus 100/((n_cell + 100) N) through the global rate
subscribe_rate_by_dow_month.smoothing: k = 100 toward the global rate of the fit rows (every fit row's label)

subscribe_rate_by_euribor_bin.apply: pd.cut(euribor3m, the stored categories, include_lowest=True) -> that bin's rate. The categories carry rounded edges, so a row near an edge can map to a neighbouring bin of the one its own fit assigned it
subscribe_rate_by_euribor_bin.fallback: outside the stored categories (or an empty bin): the median of the bin rates, i.e. the mean label of the middle bin, or the average of the two middle bins' rates
subscribe_rate_by_euribor_bin.fit: pd.qcut(euribor3m of the fit rows, q=20, duplicates='drop') (equal-width pd.cut if qcut fails); rate = mean label of the fit rows in each bin (groupby observed=True); the IntervalIndex categories are stored
subscribe_rate_by_euribor_bin.fit_rows_in_their_own_representation: yes: a fit row's label is in its bin's rate (1/n_bin)

findings.mlp_early_stopping: The early-stopping subset (15% of each MLP fit's rows) is not isolated from the Stage 1 encoders. Its labels make up 15.0% of the optimization rows' label mass and 15.0-15.1% of the validation rows' (own label 0.061-0.126%, other validation rows 15.0%); 5,097,234/5,097,234 optimization-row encodings carry subset labels and 899,651/899,666 validation-row encodings carry their own label (row-feature encodings over 111 fits). A properly isolated internal validation split excludes the entire early-stopping subset from encoder fitting: the encoders (and scaler) are fitted on the optimization rows only, so no subset label enters any encoding, of optimization or of validation rows. The accepted fits do not do this. The effects on the stopping epoch, the predictions and the AUC are not quantified here. Separately, the outer held-out rows are isolated: they are excluded from the encoders, the scaler, the network fit and its early-stopping subset, so the tuning-fold scores, the OOF scores and the Stage 4 column are scored on encoder-held-out rows (isolation checks: outer-fold flips, call sites, accepted fits).

mlp_early_stopping.finding: The early-stopping subset (15% of each MLP fit's rows) is not isolated from the Stage 1 encoders. Its labels make up 15.0% of the optimization rows' label mass and 15.0-15.1% of the validation rows' (own label 0.061-0.126%, other validation rows 15.0%); 5,097,234/5,097,234 optimization-row encodings carry subset labels and 899,651/899,666 validation-row encodings carry their own label (row-feature encodings over 111 fits). A properly isolated internal validation split excludes the entire early-stopping subset from encoder fitting: the encoders (and scaler) are fitted on the optimization rows only, so no subset label enters any encoding, of optimization or of validation rows. The accepted fits do not do this. The effects on the stopping epoch, the predictions and the AUC are not quantified here. Separately, the outer held-out rows are isolated: they are excluded from the encoders, the scaler, the network fit and its early-stopping subset, so the tuning-fold scores, the OOF scores and the Stage 4 column are scored on encoder-held-out rows (isolation checks: outer-fold flips, call sites, accepted fits).
mlp_early_stopping.isolated_split: A properly isolated internal validation split excludes the entire early-stopping subset from encoder fitting: the encoders (and scaler) are fitted on the optimization rows only, so no subset label enters any encoding, of optimization or of validation rows. The accepted fits do not do this. The effects on the stopping epoch, the predictions and the AUC are not quantified here.
mlp_early_stopping.order: Inside every black-box MLP fit - each Optuna trial on each of the 10 outer designs, each calibration refit on an outer or inner design (oof_calibration._fit_on) and the final model - the Stage 1 encoders and scaler are fitted first, on all of that fit's rows (build_fold_designs / inner_fold_designs / the full-train engineer). Stage1MLPClassifier.fit then draws its early-stopping subset from those already-encoded rows: train_test_split(test_size=val_fraction, stratify=y, random_state), with oversampling after the split. The subset's labels were therefore among the encoders' fit labels: they enter the encodings of the optimization rows (the rows the network is trained on) and of the validation rows themselves - each validation row's own label and the other validation rows' labels.
mlp_early_stopping.outer_isolation: Separately, the outer held-out rows are isolated: they are excluded from the encoders, the scaler, the network fit and its early-stopping subset, so the tuning-fold scores, the OOF scores and the Stage 4 column are scored on encoder-held-out rows (isolation checks: outer-fold flips, call sites, accepted fits).

question: For a row being encoded, exactly which rows and labels can influence its feature value, and which of those labels could have been known at the time of contact?
scope: PR 42 Commit 3 Step 3A: encoding construction and leakage audit (training side)

checks.check: each period is one contiguous run in source order
the periods span the documented range
each period has one value of each monthly or quarterly indicator
the consumer price index differs between every two periods (so periods with the same month are different years)
no period has more contact days than its calendar month has weekdays
within each period the weekday advances except at most 4 week changes (a month spans at most 5 weekday weeks)

resolution.between_days_of_a_period: source order, i.e. the documented date order (weekdays advance within each week); relation later_day_same_month
resolution.between_periods: calendar order of (year, month); relation later_month
resolution.outcome_timing: unknown: the label records whether the client subscribed, not when that became known. An earlier-day label is at most plausibly known at a later contact; a same-day label is unresolved; a later-day label was not yet known
resolution.training_rows_only: the index is built from training rows: a day whose contacts all fell in the test split is absent, which can at most merge two days with the same key into one (classified same_day, never later)
resolution.unit: contact day: a maximal run of training rows, in source order, sharing year, month, day_of_week and euribor3m (a daily rate)
resolution.within_a_day: unresolved: no time of day is recorded, so contacts of the same day are treated as simultaneous; relation same_day
resolution.year: inferred: 2008 at the first row, plus one wherever the month decreases in source order
